methodological_eligibility.evidence_quote: The purpose of this research is to experimentally study the combustion of composite slurries from industrial waste, accumulated in abandoned industrial regions, especially the Arctic and the Extreme North.

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Does not present, propose, evaluate, or critique an EnPI/EnB energy-performance-measurement model in the ISO 50001/50006 sense. It is an experimental combustion and ecological-emissions assessment of waste-derived slurry fuels (CWS/CWSP): it determines fuel combustion characteristics (ignition delay, threshold/maximum temperatures, heat of combustion) and NOx/SOx emissions, then ranks fuels against coal with an MCDM weighted-product composite index. The protocol excludes MCDM/decision-support scores from EnPI composite-index model content, and no energy baseline or relevant-variable normalisation of an energy-consuming entity is constructed; 'energy performance indicators' here are fuel-comparison ratios (incidental use of the phrase).

paper_type.evidence_quote: Laboratory experiments with such slurry fuels have been conducted.

stage1.notes: 'Energy performance indicators' here = fuel-comparison ratios + MCDM weighted-product composite index, not an ISO 50006 EnPI/EnB model of an energy-consuming entity. Application is Arctic decentralised power/heat supply, outside the closed continuous-process list.
